newsitem.title: USA: SBC starts local landline outside region.
newsitem.headline: SBC starts local landline outside region.

text.p: SBC Communications Inc said Monday its Cellular One property in Rochester, N.Y., is marketing local landline telephone service, making it a full-service telecommunications provider in that city.

This also marks the first time a former Regional Bell Operating Company, through an affiliate, has offered local landline service outside of its traditional multi-state region since the 1984 divestiture, SBC said.
Cellular One is now providing Rochester residents with local and long-distance wireless service, paging, Internet access, as well as local and long distance landline service.

"We're the first former (Regional Bell Operating Company) to offer local service outside of our traditional service area and to build a one-stop shopping center for telecommunications services," Stan Sigman, president of Southwestern Bell Mobile Systems, said in a statement. Sigman has responsibility for Cellular One.
SBC said Cellular One expects to add local service to other cities in New York State including Buffalo, Syracuse and Albany during 1997.

It added that the Cellular One affiliate in Illinois also has received approval from the Illinois Commerce Commission to offer local service in Chicago. It must still file local service tariffs and finalize marketing plans before offering the service.
"SBC appears to be using wireless as a way of selling customers a complete package (of local and long distance services)," Michael Elling of Prudential Securities said.

SBC said it expects that eventually it will offer "one-stop shopping" for telecommunications services throughout its traditional five-state service area of Missouri, Arkansas, Texas, Kansas and Oklahoma through its operating subsidiaries to consumers in all of its markets.
The company said it recently added Internet access in several cities and is offering long-distance service for its wireless customers.
"We expect to offer landline long-distance for customers in our traditional service areas by the third quarter of 1997, pending regulatory approval," Sigman said.
